## Ukraine’s MICH-2000 Drone Breaks Cover

The social media sphere is abuzz with rare footage confirming the operational use of the MICH-2000 drone in the ongoing conflict. Viral clips show the system navigating a dense wall of Russian air-defense fire to strike the Moscow Oil Refinery, marking a significant transition from operational security to public visibility. Previously kept under strict cover by the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU), this long-range strike drone’s successful deployment has led analysts to speculate that other classified assets, such as the Palianytsia or Bars drones, may have also been involved in the operation. The footage highlights not just the drone’s performance, but the evolving transparency of Ukraine’s deep-strike capabilities.

## The Great AI Tap-Out

A philosophical shift in human interaction is underway, as users debate moving from algorithmic social media feeds to direct engagement with Artificial Intelligence. Evidence for this trend includes a reported 99.5% drop in Stack Overflow traffic and the rise of "zero-click search," where users get answers without clicking through to social platforms. Zach Weinersmith suggests that exiting "The Algorithm" for non-corporate AI may offer a superior experience, particularly for tutoring, while ChosunOne warns that the danger to humanity scales with AI’s capability gap. Interestingly, critics are also challenging the "AI war" narrative, noting that conquest might be less appealing to advanced AI than simply purchasing or participating in human society.

## Souls in the Machine

Bluesky users are keeping alive a spirited debate on the philosophy of mind, specifically regarding whether AI can possess "souls." Driven by the persistent "Philosophy of Mind 101" lessons from user @SE Gyges, the discussion has moved past binary takes. While many argue either that souls are real and AI lacks them, or that souls are non-existent, @Pwnallthethings critiques this lack of nuance. The dominant counter-argument invites users to explore the "fun quadrants" of dualism, such as the idea that souls exist but are exclusive to AI, or that an individual’s specific AI might possess a soul despite general skepticism. It is a playful, persistent attempt to resolve a 3,000-year-old debate in the context of modern technology.

## Toronto’s Wild Hornets

The Ukrainian community in Toronto is rallying around the "Wild Hornets," a volunteer support group associated with the Armed Maidaan organization. Identical posts from the @SpecialKhersonCat account have circulated, inviting attendees to visit their stand at the upcoming Toronto Ukrainian Festival this weekend. The coordinated push aims to foster personal connections and support for the group’s work, serving as a grassroots effort to engage the local diaspora before the event begins.

## FAW’s Frustrated Commute

In the Female Alone with a Guy (FAW) group, user @fools_set_the_rules recounted a chaotic ride home with a male coworker. After driving in the wrong direction—allegedly due to a misheard address or intentional mischief—the driver grew angry over wasted gas. He attempted to touch her breast and kiss her; when she pushed his hand away as if punching, he admitted his sexual aggression stemmed from frustration and dropped her off on the side of the street. The post highlights unexpected sexual aggression in a professional setting and the user’s decisive, physical reaction.

## Quick Hits

*   **KDE Customization:** KDE users are sharing tips on replicating the corner-styling effects popularized by YouTuber ezkuu100, focusing on border tricks for window decorations.
*   **4chan’s Romantic Type:** A thread on WMAF discussions highlights a specific affinity for Jewish men, with comments noting the perceived genetic predisposition to schizophrenia lived up to internet expectations.
*   **Retro Tech Revival:** Mastodon user @Neliger celebrated the return of the Samsung NC110 netbook ("Patate 2") with a PeerTube video, appealing to the vintage computing community.
*   **Touhou Art:** A single, affectionate fan art piece of Yukari Yakumo blowing a kiss is circulating within the Touhou Project fandom.
*   **Camera Gear Philosophy:** On 4chan’s /gear/ board, the consensus remains that "gear only matters if your photo doesn't suck," with users humorously comparing items to the criticized "snoy" bag.
*   **Sega’s Aggressive Marketing:** A discussion on 16-bit era advertising characterizes Sega’s strategy as insecure bullying, contrasting their "perverted" and angry tone with competitors’ composed branding.

representative_texts: @Chris Kohler (kohler.bsky.social) — Last (?) curry of the trip - the "European style" katsu curry from the Jinbocho shop called Ethiopia. Looks very simple but the flavor and mouthfeel are amazing, similar to Bondy or other "European" style places.  This one's right in Ochanomizu station, in the underground dining area.

@Chris Kohler (kohler.bsky.social) — All true, but what's known as "European-style curry" in Japan is basically a Japanese invention - they applied classical European cooking techniques and ingredients to curry to create this unique style. Uses a lot of butter, veal stock, other ingredients not usually present.
context_texts: @Miss👾Eri👾chan! ☭🇺🇦🇵🇸8️⃣6️⃣4️⃣7️⃣ (misserichan.bsky.social) — "European style" might actually sort of fit. England took curry from India, and then spread it to Japan during the Meiji restoration, so Brtish curry at least is a thing. There's a Japanese brand of curry powder called Vermont Curry, even

representative_texts: @Zach Weinersmith (zachweinersmith.bsky.social) — I don't have a lot of intuition about this, but it doesn't seem obviously *worse* to me if people check out of The Algorithm and into AI. Especially if at some point we get very powerful non-corporate AI.

@ChosunOne (chosunone.io) — I think the danger is proportional to the difference in capabilities. I think you are right for near-peer level of AI intelligence. But if it becomes so capable that we can't mount effective resistance, then there's a real danger it decides our opinion doesn't matter.
context_texts: @Zach Weinersmith (zachweinersmith.bsky.social) — But I also wonder about for example people who do scicomm videos. Some of those you couldn't replace with AI (yet) but for something like teaching intro to linear algebra, having Claude tutor you is pretty excellent.

@Zach Weinersmith (zachweinersmith.bsky.social) — This is already happening on a certain level with "zero click search," but one thing I wonder about during to next few years is if we'll get people tapping out of social media, and possibly the traditional Internet in general, to just talk to AI.  Stackoverflow is 99.5% down from peak traffic.

@Doll (dollspace.gay) — A serious weakness in the “sufficiently intelligent AI inevitably wages war on humanity” story is that it needs to explain why conquest beats purchasing, contracting, and participating.
clusters.summary: The cluster discusses the potential shift of human interaction from social media algorithms to direct engagement with Artificial Intelligence, a trend evidenced by Stack Overflow’s traffic dropping 99.5% and the rise of "zero-click search." Zach Weinersmith suggests that exiting "The Algorithm" for non-corporate AI may not be worse than the current status quo, while highlighting AI’s efficacy in tutoring and the possibility of social media tap-out. In contrast, ChosunOne argues that the danger to humans is proportional to AI's capability gap, fearing that vastly superior AI might render human opinions irrelevant. Additionally, the posts critique the "AI war on humanity" narrative by questioning why conquest would be preferable to purchasing or participating in human society.
